clue.text: Transport from Hastings to hustings?

blocks.note: surface reading: a coach trip from a seaside town in Sussex to an election meeting
setter's reading: Hastings is the most famous battle in English history, so the vehicle takes its name from fighting and carries a candidate round the hustings

explanation.surface: A traveller asks how to get from a Sussex seaside town to a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Hustings are election meetings; a party's touring campaign coach is named after a battle, and Hastings is the battle of 1066, so the two words differ by one vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: The campaign coach carrying a party leader around the country during an election is a familiar British piece of political transport.

clue.text: Animal on which to venture about a shilling?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the wager's letters are wrapped around the following pair

blocks.note: to venture money is to bet
taken as written
s was the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin worth twelve pence

explanation.surface: A punter wonders which racehorse to risk a shilling on.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is any creature, especially a four-legged one, so it is a straightforward synonym for an animal.

clue.text: Victorian mathematician in pursuit of fox turned due north on time

definitions.note: a cryptic hint read literally: tod is an old word for fox, so a tod-hunter pursues one

indicators.note: something turned has been twisted round, so the compass phrase's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A Victorian academic sets off on a fox hunt, turning his horse due north at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Todhunter wrote standard Victorian mathematics textbooks. His surname splits as TOD (a dialect word for fox) and HUNTER, so the clue also describes him literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Todhunter was an English mathematician of the nineteenth century, famous for textbooks on algebra, calculus and the history of probability.

clue.text: Come down from odd holes with a number

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of order, so the letters of the word holes are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
eight is one particular number

explanation.surface: A golfer descends after playing some strange holes on the course.
explanation.walkthrough: Holes and a number suggest a golf course; the number is a specific one, and it joins the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft or bird that drops lower in the sky is said to descend, which is exactly what this phrase describes.

clue.text: 12 piece of wood that should have been done

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: a pile of work that should have been done

blocks.note: the answer to 12 across is a rear row; rear means back
a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A stick from the back of the woodpile was overlooked when the chores were finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 12, whose first word REAR is read as BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished tasks that have piled up are an accumulation of arrears; that accumulation is the answer.

clue.text: Thomas Carlyle's head in a tank

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter, so only Carlyle's opening letter is used
in places that single letter inside the word for the tank

blocks.note: a septic tank, the sewage tank of a house without mains drainage; the selected letter goes inside after SEP
the first letter of the name Carlyle

explanation.surface: The Victorian historian Thomas Carlyle has his head stuck in a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Carlyle looks like one person, but Thomas is the definition: doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the resurrection without proof.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas doubted until he saw the wounds, so his name is a byword for a doubter or disbeliever.

clue.text: Some are muscling in on being suckled by a wolf

definitions.note: a participle phrase standing for the one being suckled

indicators.note: some means a part of the following words, so the letters run on inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of are and the start of muscling

explanation.surface: Interlopers muscle in on a wolf's cubs at feeding time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman legend the twins Romulus and Remus were suckled by a she-wolf.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus and his twin brother were abandoned as babies and fed by a she-wolf before founding Rome in the legend.

clue.text: See 24
Episcopal joint

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the noun: the bishop's headdress

blocks.note: first meaning: the tall pointed hat worn by a bishop
second meaning: a corner joint in carpentry made from two pieces cut at forty-five degrees

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a joint smoked by a bishop or a cathedral's roast; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The bishop's tall headdress and the carpenter's angled corner joint share one name in English.

clue.text: Spooner to get hold of cheese - it comes to land

definitions.note: a clause standing for the thing that comes ashore

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words are exchanged

blocks.note: to get hold of is to seize and Brie is a soft French cheese; swap the opening sounds of seize Brie

explanation.surface: Someone is told to grab some cheese before it arrives on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: Brie seize, with B-R and S swapped, says the two words of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: During the day, cooler air flows from the ocean onto the shore, so this wind is one that comes in to land.

clue.text: Range with directions

blocks.note: and joins things, as with does
E and S, east and south, are two compass directions

explanation.surface: A cooker comes with an instruction leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: Range wants to be a kitchen stove and directions a set of instructions; it is a mountain range and two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American mountain chain running down the western side of the continent is a range.

clue.text: Needlewoman embroidering a top with right lace

indicators.note: embroidering works threads into a new pattern, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A seamstress decorates a blouse with lace.
explanation.walkthrough: Needlewoman looks like a seamstress, but it is the woman with a Needle: Cleopatra's Needle is an Egyptian obelisk on the Thames Embankment in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient obelisk on London's Embankment bears the Egyptian queen's name, making her, playfully, the woman of that Needle.

clue.text: Hallmarked piece of pewter makes sense on South American river

blocks.note: touch is one of the five senses
the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: Silversmith's jargon: a stamped pewter item gives you a feel for a river in Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewterers registered their maker's marks by striking them on a guild record plate, so the piece carries each stamped mark.

clue.text: Don't start long journey round Scots island from the back row

indicators.note: not starting means the word for the journey loses its first letter
round means going about, so what remains of the journey wraps the island

blocks.note: a trek is a long, arduous journey
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone is advised against setting out round a Scottish island from the back of a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: From the back looks like a reversal instruction; it is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a military formation or a theatre, the line of people furthest behind is the rear row.

clue.text: Act I - our act - shows domineering

indicators.note: a show stages material in a fresh form, so the preceding letters are put on in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A theatre company boasts that its first act proves how bossy it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules alone with absolute power, so behaviour like that ruler's is bossy and overbearing.

clue.text: Brought the other Dutch firm for tunnel construction: it's lying at the limit

annotation.answer: NOTHING COULD BE FURTHER FROM THE TRUTH

blocks.clueFragment: Brought the other Dutch firm for tunnel construction
blocks.note: surface reading: a claim that a rival Dutch contractor was hired to build a tunnel, the kind of report a spokesman flatly denies
setter's reading: the phrase is the strongest possible way of saying a statement is false, a lie taken as far as it goes

explanation.surface: A press report says a different Dutch company was hired to dig a tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a sample allegation for the stock denial to answer; the second half defines the phrase as untruth at its extreme.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock rebuttal declares a claim to be as false as anything could possibly be, the very limit of untruth.

clue.text: One bird's note on marsh raised by 10's predecessor

definitions.note: the answer to 10 is the last queen of Egypt, Cleopatra

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read upwards, so the pieces run from bottom to top

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tit is a small songbird
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a fen is low marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens

explanation.surface: A bird sings a note over the marshes, lifted up by an ancient queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The four pieces read ITITREFEN and are turned round. The cross-reference to 10 points to Cleopatra, who reigned long after this earlier Egyptian queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefertiti was queen of Egypt under Akhenaten, over a thousand years before Cleopatra, so she came earlier as a famous Egyptian queen.

clue.text: Obliged to make a tax leap

blocks.note: a duty is a tax on goods
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: Someone is forced into a sudden jump in taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone required by moral or legal obligation to act is compelled, which is what obliged means here.

clue.text: River bird spilling his wine

indicators.note: spilling throws things about, so the letters of his are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
a hen is a bird
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A bird by the river knocks over a man's glass of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish is an old name for wine from the Rhine valley in Germany, so it names a type of wine.

clue.text: Hollywood has a dog's name, keeping left, mile on mile

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the dog's name holds the next two letters

blocks.note: Fido is the traditional name for a dog; it splits as FI and DO around the inserted letters
L is the abbreviation for left
M is the abbreviation for mile
a second mile, M, added at the end

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star's dog keeps to the left as it walks mile after mile.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is used as shorthand for the whole American film industry, the world of the movies.

clue.text: See 12
South African by birth

blocks.note: first meaning: the former province of South Africa
second meaning: an adjective for things relating to being born

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one description of someone's nationality; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a South African region and is also the adjective relating to childbirth, as in antenatal.

clue.text: Very bad beer - old pal's drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk is all over the place, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A disgusting pint has left an old friend the worse for wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deserving strong condemnation or regret is shockingly poor, which is what very bad means.

clue.text: Solver's in line for alcohol

indicators.note: in places the solver's possessive inside the word for the line

blocks.note: an el is an elevated railway line in an American city; it splits around the inserted word
the setter addresses the solver as thou, so the solver's is thy

explanation.surface: A crossword solver queues for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl alcohol, or ethanol, is the alcohol in drinks, so the chemical name stands for alcohol.

clue.text: Guy with 10, a figure of speech

blocks.note: the number 10 read as a word, not a cross-reference
a trope is a figure of speech such as a metaphor

explanation.surface: A man stands with the Egyptian queen of 10, turning a phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like a cross-reference to Cleopatra, as in other clues here; this time it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a cord or line that holds a tent steady, pegged into the ground.

clue.text: Dylan's answer is coming soon

definitions.note: the answer is blowin' in the wind in Bob Dylan's song

blocks.note: first meaning: where Bob Dylan's song places the answer, my friend
second meaning: an idiom for something about to happen

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a promise that the singer will reply shortly; the song line and the idiom are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An event that is about to take place or is rumoured to be on its way is said to be imminent in this idiom.

clue.text: See 14
Eyot has a tenant

blocks.note: a property that has a tenant is rented out; split into two words, a verb and a participle

explanation.surface: A small river island is rented out to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot is a small island in a river, a word common on the Thames; the wordplay reads as IS LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a small island, the river one being a regional English term.

clue.text: Call motorway police: a learner's causing a fatality

blocks.note: ho is a call to attract attention
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as I
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
taken as written
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Get the traffic police: a learner driver on the motorway has killed someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the killing of a person, so behaviour that is murderous in that way results in a death.
